title: Family DNS Guard Now Logs Every Device's Sites | vitalii.no
description:
How the family DNS guard went from blindly filtering requests to logging exactly which sites and IPs every device talked to, including Android phones that only support Private DNS.

The guard could already filter DNS requests, but it couldn't tell me what a device had actually been visiting, and Android devices using Private DNS (DoT) instead of DoH weren't covered at all. The id-to-MAC mapping only came from a static environment-variable fallback, with no way to see or add which devices were even connected.

I added Android Private DNS support, so a device now connects through its own subdomain and the id-to-MAC mapping comes from a live agent endpoint instead of a hardcoded fallback. On the data side, two new Cloudflare database tables track every hit by device and day, with service name, resolved IPs, first and last seen timestamps and a hit count, plus a reverse table that answers "whose IP is this" from the IP alone. The dashboard got a new sites-and-IPs section with a Today and Yesterday toggle and a filter for technical domains, backed by a daily cleanup job and a cache bump so the new UI actually loads on devices that already had the old one installed.

The result: I can open the dashboard, pick a kid's device, and see the real list of domains and IPs it talked to for the last two days — Android phones included.
